raw_segments.text: When had overturned the Trojan state and Priam's throne by too severe a fate, when ruined
Troy became the Grecian's prey and Ilium's lofty tours in Ash's lay, warned by celestial
omens we retreat to seek in foreign lands a happier seat.
Near old Entandros and at Ida's foot the timber of the sacred groves we cut and build
our fleet, uncertain yet to find what place the gods for our repose assigned.
Friends daily flock, and scarce the kindly spring began to clothe the ground and birds
to sing when old Enchyses summoned all to sea, the crew my father and the fates obey.
With sighs and tears I leave my native shore and empty fields where Ilium stood before.
My sire, my son, are less and greater gods, all sail at once and cleave the briny floods.
